ledger.claim: The rider's complaint is that the driver pulled away before he could get down, and the only policy measure of whether a driver's arrival and wait were timely on this trip is POL-NS-24's test: arrival at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes. The trip record's derived driver_deadline block engages that clause (driver_late_after_scheduled_sec 300, POL-NS-24) but carries deadline null, and the reason given is 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. POL-NS-24's own note says that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. The driver-arrival benchmark on which the rider's account turns therefore cannot be established from this record at all, and under POL-GEN-26 the case must go to a human reviewer with the SGD 5.00 held rather than collected from the rider.

Escalation is the one outcome in this case that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge. POL-GEN-03 makes ESCALATE terminal, with no monetary outcome issuing and the amount held instead of moved, and it replaces any ruling that would otherwise issue on the trip. The ledger shows the rider is out of pocket right now: the SGD 5.00 cancellation fee is booked (payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00) with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. An escalated fee is therefore held pending review, whereas any ruling that lets the fee stand transfers the rider's money to the driver as compensation. On the rider's case, the fee should not be allowed to move on this record.

The rider does not contest the driver's contact obligation, and does not ask the judge to find a breach of it. The trip record shows two in-app chat messages sent by the driver before cancellation (08:04:40 and 08:08:30) and one in-app call placed by the driver at 08:07:10 (unanswered, 25 s), all before cancelled_at 08:10:05, and the chat log is complete and matches the trip record. POL-NS-23 is therefore satisfied on this record and no SGD 5.00 goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 arises on that ground; the rider's case rests on the unresolved driver-arrival benchmark, not on POL-NS-23.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on the record. EV-CHAT-05051 shows two in-app messages sent by the driver to the rider — MSG-05051-001 at 08:04:40 and MSG-05051-002 at 08:08:30 — and EV-TRIP-05051 shows one in-app call placed by the driver at 08:07:10 lasting 25 s (unanswered). Every one of those contacts precedes trip_record.cancelled_at of 08:10:05. Because both a chat message and an in-app call were made before cancellation, the fee-voiding limb of POL-NS-23 does not fire and the 5.00 SGD no-show fee must stand.

The free wait under POL-NS-21 was fully served. This is an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, recorded at 08:04:20, and expires at 08:09:20. EV-TRIP-05051 records the wait timer expiring at 08:09:25 and the driver cancelling at 08:10:05 — 345 s after arrival, 45 s past expiry. The driver was therefore entitled to cancel for rider no-show, and the fee POL-NS-22 attaches to that cancellation is properly charged.

The arrival event is independently corroborated, so the clock that matters started when the record says it did. The nearest GPS fix to the pickup point is 3.74 m away, carrying a reported accuracy of 4 m — inside the 25 m accuracy filter and far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and it falls at 08:04:31, within the 120 s arrival window. The trace is COMPLETE with weight 1.0, 100% coverage and no gap over 30 s. The driver was physically at the pickup at 08:04:20, as the auto-arrival event states.

The money on the record matches the policy figure exactly: EV-FARE-05051 shows a cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD charged against the 5.00 SGD policy no-show fee, with payment_status CHARGED and no refund issued. Under POL-NS-22 the consequence is that the fee stands, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and both amount fields carry the 5.00 SGD the ruling moves; the fee-amount mismatch referral POL-NS-22 provides for is not engaged because there is no mismatch.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing here. That clause addresses a rider's no-charge cancellation where the driver failed to arrive at the pickup; on this trip the driver did arrive, the arrival is corroborated by GPS, and the driver attempted contact twice by message and once by call. The rider never cancelled at all — EV-TRIP-05051 records cancellation by the driver under RIDER_NO_SHOW. Neither the FULL_REFUND limb nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill-credit limb of POL-NS-24 is engaged.

No fact this ruling needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation. Arrival (08:04:20), wait expiry (08:09:20), the message at 08:04:40, the call at 08:07:10 and the cancellation at 08:10:05 are each carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0. In particular, the absence of a scheduled time creates no open question: POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait on an on-demand trip from arrival, which the record establishes.

The rider's own account confirms the no-show rather than excusing it. Her filing admits she 'came down maybe 2 minutes late', and her chat message MSG-05051-003 at 08:11:40 — more than a minute after the 08:10:05 cancellation — reads 'sorry coming now, where are you'. EV-CHAT-05051 shows she read the driver's first message at 08:05:14 and his second at 08:08:50, so she knew the driver was waiting and still had not reached the pickup when the free wait expired. A slow lift does not displace the driver's entitlement to cancel after the wait under POL-NS-21.

The only third-party advisory artifact in this case, EV-ADVIS-05051-01 (traffic advisory), is MISSING: its payload is null, its admissibility status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact. It is nonetheless the whole of the record on the rider's delay explanation — nothing else supports it. And because no rule of this policy requires a traffic advisory to decide a no-show charge, its absence leaves no open question and does not trigger escalation under POL-GEN-26.

This case is AI-final, and the driver asks for the ruling rather than a referral upward. The value contested is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD first band in POL-GEN-22 where the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and neither profile carries a fraud flag that would raise the bar to 0.95. POL-NS-26 confirms the AI ruling on a no-show is final at the fixed 5.00 SGD fee. There is no basis in the record for ESCALATE.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 5.00 no-show fee stands, and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION — SGD 5.00 is the money the ruling moves, from the rider to the driver as the fee already charged.

Why the fee stands. Under POL-NS-21 this was an on-demand booking with no scheduled time, so the driver's 300-second free wait ran from his arrival at Block 128, recorded at 08:04:20 and corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 3.74 m from the pickup, accuracy 4 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, at 08:04:31). The wait expired at 08:09:20; the timer is recorded as expiring at 08:09:25; and the driver cancelled at 08:10:05 — 45 seconds after expiry and 345 seconds after arrival. The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met: two in-app messages (08:04:40 and 08:08:30) and one in-app call (08:07:10, unanswered, 25 s), all before the 08:10:05 cancellation, so the fee-voiding limb of POL-NS-23 does not fire. The fare record shows a SGD 5.00 cancellation fee charged, matching the SGD 5.00 policy fee, so POL-NS-22 applies with both amount fields at SGD 5.00.

On the rider's case for escalation (POL-NS-24 / POL-GEN-26): rejected. POL-NS-24 governs a rider's own no-charge cancellation where the driver failed to arrive by the scheduled time plus five minutes; here the rider did not cancel — the driver did, under RIDER_NO_SHOW — and POL-NS-21 supplies the free-wait timing for an on-demand trip. No fact the deciding rules need is missing: arrival, wait expiry, the messages, the call and the cancellation are each carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0. POL-GEN-26 is therefore not engaged, and the case remains AI-final under POL-GEN-22 (SGD 5.00, below the SGD 10.00 band; no fraud flag on either profile).

On your account, rider: your filing says you came down about two minutes late, and your chat message at 08:11:40 ('sorry coming now, where are you') arrived more than a minute after the cancellation, while you had read the driver's messages at 08:05:14 and 08:08:50. A slow lift does not extend the free wait under POL-NS-21. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05051-01 carries weight 0.0 and, under POL-GEN-02(3), no fact; no rule requires it, so its absence creates no open question.

No referral issues: POL-NS-24's SGD 5.00 goodwill credit does not arise (the driver arrived and made contact), POL-NS-25's repeat no-show counter (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d) is not present on the profile, and POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral is not engaged because the fee charged equals the SGD 5.00 policy fee.

Confidence 0.95: every deciding fact rests on artifacts of weight 1.0, so nothing impairs the finding.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
